First of all, congratulation on becoming a father\! :partying_face:

Starting from 2020 June all fathers (or fathers to be) can request 30 days of paternity leave until the child turns 3 years old. To do that then please register your requested dated from our [Social Insurance Board e-service |https://iseteenindus.sotsiaalkindlustusamet.ee/dashboard/portal/login?url=%2Fdashboard%2Fportal]system. Please notify your manager about the leave beforehand so they can organise teams work accordingly 😉 (at least 14 days ahead).

All 30 days are compensated by our Social Insurance Board and the exact amount how much you’ll get for this period depends on your income you had 9 months ago. There’s also a [calculator|https://www.kalkulaator.ee/et/vanemahuvitise-kalkulaator] that you can use to calculate the approximate amount (unfortunately it’s only in Estonian). Please note that they will transfer you the money at the beginning of next month you take the leave (by 8th calendar day).

When requesting the days then please know that you can take all days out at once or you can take these out in parts. But keep in mind that paternity leave is calculated in calendar days, so if you include weekend days then these will also be counted as your paternity leave days.

{noformat}WITH courier_balance as (SELECT date_trunc('day',CONVERT_TIMEZONE(act.timezone, b.created)) as dates, a.external_id AS Courier_ID, a.currency, 
								sum(b.amount) as daily_total, 
								sum(CASE WHEN b.external_type IN ('cashPayment') THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) as cashpayments,
								sum(CASE WHEN b.external_type IN ('payment', 'paymentReversion') THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) as payments,
								sum(CASE WHEN b.external_type = 'bonus' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END) as bonus,
								sum(CASE WHEN b.external_type IN ('smallOrderFee','delivery') THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END ) as DeliveryTotal,
								sum(CASE WHEN b.external_type = 'deposit' THEN b.amount ELSE 0 END ) as Deposit
						 FROM payout.invoicing_balance_account as a
						 JOIN payout.invoicing_balance_balance_entry as b
						 ON a.id = b.account_id AND a.type = 'food_courier' 
						 LEFT JOIN admin_system_city as act on act.id = b.city_id 
						 GROUP BY 1,2,3
                         ORDER BY dates DESC ), 
daily_balance as ( SELECT DISTINCT *, sum(daily_total) OVER (PARTITION BY Courier_ID
				   ORDER BY dates, Courier_ID rows between unbounded PRECEDING and current ROW) as aggregated_sum
				   FROM courier_balance
				   ORDER BY dates desc),
courier_calendar_dates as ( SELECT * FROM (SELECT external_id, currency AS cur
							FROM payout.invoicing_balance_account
							WHERE type = 'food_courier')
							CROSS JOIN (SELECT date, year, month FROM public.dim_calendar dc
							WHERE date > '2019-01-01' and date < CURRENT_DATE)),
snapshot_balance as (SELECT *,  CASE WHEN aggregated_sum IS NULL THEN LAG(aggregated_sum, 1) IGNORE NULLS OVER (PARTITION BY external_id order by date ASC) ELSE aggregated_sum END AS lastvalue
					, CASE WHEN lastvalue < 0 THEN 1 ELSE NULL END as Datedif 
					FROM courier_calendar_dates as ccd 
					LEFT JOIN daily_balance as db ON ccd.external_id = db.Courier_ID and ccd.date = db.dates and ccd.cur = db.currency 
					ORDER BY ccd.date DESC),
running_totals as (SELECT *, SUM(datedif) IGNORE NULLS OVER (PARTITION BY external_id ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) as counter 
					FROM snapshot_balance),
outstandingdays as (SELECT *,
			CASE WHEN Datedif IS NOT NULL THEN ROW_NUMBER () OVER (PARTITION BY external_id, c - d ORDER BY date) ELSE NULL END AS outstanding_days		
			FROM (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER () OVER (ORDER BY external_id, date) as c,									
									ROW_NUMBER () OVER (PARTITION BY external_id, COALESCE(datedif, 0) ORDER BY date) as d
									FROM running_totals)),
Conversion_period as (SELECT *, LEAD(date, 1) over (PARTITION BY external_id ORDER BY date) as next_period
                FROM outstandingdays as od),
final_table as (SELECT lp.*, COALESCE(r.rate,1) as exchange_rate, r.valid_on as exchange_rate_valid_on, 
				COALESCE(cashpayments,0) as cashpayments_received,
				COALESCE(daily_total,0) as daily_total_received,
				COALESCE(payments,0) as payments_received,
				COALESCE(bonus,0) as bonus_received,
				COALESCE(DeliveryTotal,0) as DeliveryAmount_received,
				COALESCE(Deposit,0) as BagDeposit
				FROM Conversion_period as lp
				LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates AS r on r.currency = lp.cur
				AND DATE(r.valid_on) = dateadd(day, -1,next_period)
				WHERE r.valid_on is not null 
				ORDER BY date desc)
SELECT external_id, date, daily_total_received, payments_received, cashpayments_received, bonus_received, DeliveryAmount_received, BagDeposit, lastvalue

There are no specific requirements concerning the place of residence or nationality of the Director. However, if the company intends to employ foreigner, it must obtain relevant work permit. The whole procedure of obtaining the work permit may take about 1.5 months. This is rather technical process, thus far a denial would be rather extraordinary event. In regard to citizens of Armenia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Russia no work permit is required.

As for place of residence, such situation when the Director is almost always outside Belarus occurs in our practice. But a number of practical implications of such distant work should be taken into account (e.g., execution of the documents, including accounting and payment documents, representation of the company’s interests in relations with third parties, state authorities and company’s employees, etc.). To a certain extent it may be resolved by issuing the power of attorney to a loyal local employee of the company, so there will a person able to sign documents necessary for day-to-day activities when the Director is abroad.

However, please keep in mind the following potential legal implications of such arrangement:

 

* _legal uncertainty of such set-up_: in particular, in case of unusual/controversial situation with the Director (for example, the need to bring him to liability by Belarusian company), there may be difficulties given the lack of local court practice in resolving labour disputes, when the labour activity was in fact permanently performed outside of Belarus;
* _tax issues_: risk of double taxation of the Director’s remuneration needs to be assessed. Also potential permanent establishment (*PE*) implications outside Belarus need to be considered due to signing on the territory of foreign country of the documents by the Director of Belarusian company in the interests of this Belarusian company. Therefore we would suggest to request tax and PE risk evaluation under the domestic law of the respective country;
* _inconsistency of factual circumstances with what is on paper_: Generally the role of the Director implies that he/she has to work in employer’s office a significant part of the time. So we believe there are no grounds for formalising official remote work for the Director. It means that there will be ordinary employment agreement with regular working place. In its turn it means that with regard to the Director who is a foreigner with the work permit there may be questions from the part of the migration authority due to such inconsistency. Please also note that for the Director who is foreigner with the work permit and who is always (or principally) on unpaid social leave, there is a high risk that the subsequent extension of the work permit is denied (since the migration authority may consider that the appointment of a foreign director is inappropriate).

On theory , the GDPR art 22 states

_“The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling,_ *_which produces legal effects concerning him or her_* _or_ *_similarly significantly affects him or her_*_.”_

So this is of course matter of debate but I would rather be cautious and see that this applies since the decision of blocking will be based solely on automated processing and it will produce a significant effect concerning him/her , meaning that he/she cannot use a service they signed up for. In guidelines, it is stated that processing can significantly affect you if it influences your circumstances, behaviour or choices. So, I would take a more high-level approach here. However, I may consult with ICO, for example and ask whether blocking a service would be included here. 

Article 22 then goes on

_“Paragraph 1 shall not apply if the decision: (a) is necessary for entering into, or performance of, a contract between the data subject and a data controller;_

So, if we do accept that the decision may significantly affect the user, then we need to justify that it is needed for the performance of the contract with the user. 

And finally, if we manage to do this, then article 22 also adds that 

_“In the cases referred to in points (a) and (c) of paragraph 2, the data controller shall implement suitable measures to safeguard the data subject's rights and freedoms and legitimate interests, at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision.”_

So, this is where the human intervention comes in. Meaning that if we have established that article 22 applies and the processing is needed for performance of contract, then we need to provide the right for human review for the decision made. 

The guidelines see that if we use automated decision-making for performance of contract, then a DPIA should also be carried out. Which I agree. So, if we definitely want to go on with this, then I would approach a external counsel asap and ask for a DPIA. What do you think?

* How to design the test?

----

h3. Where to collect the ideas?

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UlgaxTB7Z1ZEyPXl9rX6W4bpRpOkm4ZTJxvHGeAAsEU/edit#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UlgaxTB7Z1ZEyPXl9rX6W4bpRpOkm4ZTJxvHGeAAsEU/edit#gid=0|smart-link] (_Ideas_ tab) - the tracker can be used for tests in 2021.

The information needed: user type, description, examples of the articles to be included in the test. It may be useful to include the information on the possible impact (either higher deflection rate or report accuracy).

----

h3. Where to track the progress of the tests?

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UlgaxTB7Z1ZEyPXl9rX6W4bpRpOkm4ZTJxvHGeAAsEU/edit#gid=900281289|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1UlgaxTB7Z1ZEyPXl9rX6W4bpRpOkm4ZTJxvHGeAAsEU/edit#gid=900281289|smart-link] (_Content A/B test tracker_ tab) - the tracker can be used for tests in 2021.

The tracker is organised to accommodate future needs but can be modified as per the needs. The current organisation is based on other available A/B test trackers used in the company.

----

h3. Where to get ideas for tests from?

* Evaluation of how a certain type of content or visuals in the self-help work (e.g. visuals in the article)
* Potentially unhealthy self-help articles flagged by Looker reports (WIP)
* Requests or ideas from the stakeholders

----

h3. How to evaluate ideas and prioritise them?

* Identify the rough effort and impact from the change to test to calculate ROI
** ROI = impact/effort
* To identify the impact, we may check the result we expect:
** For example, the number of views of the articles in question and the number of tickets we may deflect with the change
* We may take some of the ideas with low ROI if the results are needed for a better understanding of the rider needs and search patterns or of how each type of content works

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*The easy tips to go with:*

* Top-20 articles had ~76% of all the views in Q1
* Top-30 ATIs covered ~68% of all incoming tickets in Q1
* Top-10 languages are used for ~92% of all the self-help sessions
** In Q1: EN(US), EN(GB), RU, PL, PT, UA, AZ, RO, FR, CZ
{panel}

----

h3. What metrics to choose?

We will have the usual report on the results of each A/B test (the default number of metrics used for other tests) and additional explore in Looker.

The key metric proposed by the CS Prod team – active support deflection rate, proxied by Rider TPR and PPR.

The key metric and additional metrics will depend on the hypothesis we have.

Metrics to check (for the Looker explore) if possible:

* (Number of users who viewed the article)
* Deflection rate
* Session length
* Report accuracy rate (ATIs of the tickets submitted), if possible

The list of the additional metrics may be expanded in the future, following the task [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CMO-2312|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CMO-2312|smart-link].

----

h3. How to design the test? (TL;DR)

* Hypotheses: what effect we expect (higher deflection rate or higher report accuracy rate)
* (Additional) metrics to use: what we check before and after the test to evaluate the results (deflection rate, session length, report accuracy rate, etc.)
* Test requirements: what is tested (different title style, article structure, visuals, etc.)
* User groups: who should be included/excluded from the test
* *Practical significance, or MDE: what is the minimal level of the change we consider good from the business standpoint (mainly for us to understand with what changes to proceed)

h3. How to design the test? (More detailed version)

Ideally, we would need to define:

* *Hypotheses*
** Null hypothesis – when there is no effect due to the change
** Alternative hypothesis – when there is an effect due to the change. We will be looking into the direction of the change too (either positive or negative)

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
While thinking of an alternative hypothesis, we should think about what we are interested in: the direction of the change (positive or negative) or only positive changes (negative changes are considered as no effect).

An example to illustrate this (_a_ – control, _b_ – treatment)

* H~0~: a=b
* H~A~: a≠b or b>a
{panel}

* *Metrics to check and compare*
** We will use active support deflection rate, proxied by Rider TPR and PPR, session length, and report accuracy rate for now
* *Practical (substantive) significance or Minimum Detectable Effect value*
** The level of effect expected to see from a business point of view for the change to be valuable. It depends on the field.
** We will discuss the results case by case until we have enough data to understand what is a practical significance level optimal for us. We will also need to look into the costs of the work done for the change to understand whether the results are worth it.
*** For example, in campaigns, they use the _GMV uplift to cost ratio_ to check if the profit outstands the costs of each campaign. Practical significance levels are set for each country based on a number of conditions.
** MDE value affects the minimum sample size needed to detect such an effect.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
Usually, the statistical significance bar is lower than the practical significance bar, so that if the outcome is practically significant, it is also statistically significant.
{panel}

* *Test requirements*
** The exact changes we want to test (e.g. visuals, new titles, article structure/layout)

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Only one change at a time\! Otherwise, it may not be clear what caused the effect.
{panel}

* *User groups*
** The group(s) of users who should be included/excluded from the test (e.g. all the users except the UK)
* *Risk assessment*
** If there are any (legal) risks or ethical problems. Most probably, the potential risks will be low for all our tests.

Other steps are done by other teams (i.e. identifying significance level and sample size, identifying the test duration, sampling).

----

h3. How to interpret the results and define the next steps?

* Review the results
** Are the results are statistically and practically significant for us to make the decision?
** Can we draw any conclusion based on the results?
** Do we need any additional tests to run?
* Based on the results review, define the next steps:
** (Don’t) implement the change
** Make a note in the self-help guidelines
** Plan a new test

{noformat}root@live-ib-vttablet-105:~# cat check_vitess_backup.sh
#!/bin/bash
# NRPE exit codes
# 0 - OK
# 1 - WARNING
# 2 - CRITICAL
# 3 - UNKNOWN

# number of hours since last backup to alert on
# can also be passed as arguments, first CRITICAL then WARNING thresholds
CRIT_THRESHOLD=${1:-24}
WARN_THRESHOLD=${2:-13}

# populate Vitess specific env vars
source /etc/vitess/env.sh

# get last backup from vtctld
# will return empty string if no backups present
VTCTLD_SERVER='live-ib-vtctld-1.vt:15999'
VTCTLCLIENT="command vtctlclient -server $VTCTLD_SERVER -grpc_auth_static_client_creds /etc/vitess/grpc_static_client_auth.json"
LAST_BACKUP=$(eval $VTCTLCLIENT ListBackups $KEYSPACE/$SHARD | tail -1)

#if no backup found exit with CRITICIAL
if [ -z "$LAST_BACKUP" ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - BACKUP TEST - no backup found"
    exit 2
fi

# parse date and time
LAST_BACKUP_DATE=$(echo $LAST_BACKUP | cut -d'.' -f1)
LAST_BACKUP_TIME=$(echo $LAST_BACKUP | cut -d'.' -f2 | sed 's/.\{2\}/&:/g;s/:$//')

# calculate seconds since last seen backup
SECS_SINCE_BACKUP=$(expr $(date +'%s') - $(date -d"$LAST_BACKUP_DATE $LAST_BACKUP_TIME" +'%s'))

# exit with CRITICAL if backup age > CRIT threshold
# exit with WARNING if backup age > WARN threshold
MAX_SECS_CRIT=$(expr $CRIT_THRESHOLD \* 60 \* 60)
MAX_SECS_WARN=$(expr $WARN_THRESHOLD \* 60 \* 60)
if [ $SECS_SINCE_BACKUP -gt $MAX_SECS_CRIT ]
then
    echo "CRITICAL - BACKUP TEST - backup older then $CRIT_THRESHOLD hours"
    exit 2
elif [ $SECS_SINCE_BACKUP -gt $MAX_SECS_WARN ]
then
    echo "WARNING - BACKUP TEST - backup older then $WARN_THRESHOLD hours"
    exit 1
fi

echo "OK - BACKUP TEST - backup less than CRIT: $CRIT_THRESHOLD and WARN: $WARN_THRESHOLD hours"
exit 0
{noformat}

First, sorry for the lengthy of this response:

You are correct: facial recognition and automated decision making was implemented before a DPO (i.e. myself) was installed, and so it follows there is no DPIA for this in the context of age verification for riders either. (This process only recently came to light). At minimum, therefore, there is a technical breach of the accountability expectations in GDPR and UK GDPR. And there’s no transparency afforded in the Privacy Notice - again, another breach.

*INITIAL THOUGHTS*

The passenger age verification is less risky than for drivers because the harm is the refusal of a service akin to, let’s say, an alcohol sale where the refusal is incorrect. For drivers there was potential economic harm which meets a threshold of a legal/significant affect to the individual in the event of a ‘fail’ by Jumio.

For riders we can rely on a legal basis of contractual necessity - our terms, I assume, are clear that riders must be of a certain age? Using contract as a lawful basis  is an exemption in itself to making automated decisions. 

But it is the use of facial recognition, the inherent invasiveness of the tech, that must be demonstrated to be just in achieving the objective i.e. to corroborate a person’s age to  to engage with the service. And that’s what’s missing.

Let me take the points in turn:

*(1) The appeal mechanism*

So let me turn to Liina’s proposal first: 
I am comfortable generally with automated decisions being taken for passenger age verification*. But we need a remedial step to prevent the wrongful refusal of the service bearing in mind that the decision appears automated without human intervention (and worse still using face-rec). To deny wrongly is in itself a breach of the accuracy principle in the GDPR/UK GDPR. The selfie-ID check appears reasonable as an appeals process, to ensure accuracy/rectify inaccuracy. At FB we would do the same, and this has been justified to regulators on grounds of safeguarding children, ensuring account integrity etc etc.

If Liina’s process, described above, was for CS to undertake a manual selfie/ID check, confirm, then delete, then this, I reckon, seems a mitigation to be rolled-out - and appears very practical.

*(2) Transparency/Right to be informed*

Alex, you are again correct: bearing in mind this is ‘news’ there are none of the necessary details required in the Privacy Notice concerning ‘automated decision making’ along these lines. I have redrafted a Global Passenger Privacy Notice and can, today, create a passage in that notice on “Automated Decisions”. I’ll take that as an action for today, and we can look to publish next week:

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sM9wviA9BSXShSTdHV2q3zYL7l_ssvvFy87F0R-mwiA/edit#|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sM9wviA9BSXShSTdHV2q3zYL7l_ssvvFy87F0R-mwiA/edit#|smart-link] 

The draft, as stands, does include information on the right to object to automated decision making and for human review. This is the crucial bit, I feel. So, hence the push for Liina’s workaround on selfies above.

This can be the ‘flag’ you mentioned to customers. 

(I am unsure what, if any, information is provided to data subjects when they are presented with Jumio actions to take. Potentially we have a  UI fail, and I think OC should be given screenshots of the driver Jumio experience- but more pressing are the points you’ve already raised.)

*(3) On a DPIA for rider age verification*

And you’re right here. Once more, the use of facial recognition makes it mandatory for a DPIA because of the inherent risks associated with the technology itself - because it is to be recognised that this tech is invasive to one’s privacy.

That said, in these circumstances, it seems a very useful means, theoretically, at scale to safeguard against underage use of Bolt services, prevent the breaching of conditions, elevating safety, and meeting compliance expectations from the likes of TfL etc etc. The failure is the DPIA NOT having been done to demonstrate that the use of facial recognition, and the automated decision, was not a significant risk to fundamental rights and freedoms. Is this justified? Likely it is, but we can’t demonstrate that on paper = FAIL.

We need to do this retrospectively, of course. The risks are with the inherent intrusiveness of the facial recognition tech itself. But, again, this is far less risky than those material  risks the technology and Auto-D presented specifically to drivers should they e.g. be suspended from the platform and unable to earn. A passenger can instead use Uber, or in the event of being refused an alcohol sale, to continue the analogy, can nip next door to Tesco.

We have a backlog of retrospective DPIAs needed (e.g. passenger and driver rating function are two very pressing) and we’re beyond bandwidth. The Jumio on Drivers is a priority based on risk (and TfL asking). On receipt of the OC DPIA on Jumio/Driver, I’d reckon it would be easier to justify the use of the facial recognition in another new DPIA for Passenger Age/Jumio - its the same intrusiveness but for the protection of minors at scale with little/no economic harms. To that extent, much of the work is actually already underway by OC e.g. “risks associated with facial rec tech = x, y, z”. .  If you want the same OC to complete this task, another DPIA, bearing in mind the savings and their involvement already, I’m happy for you to approach them and ask. Otherwise, can fix in-house following the completion of the Driver/Jumio DPIA by OC.

*Next steps/decisions*


* Do we roll out the selfie verification check as an appeals mechanism, and to honour human involvement in the decision?
* Calum to update redrafted Passenger Privacy Notice on Automated Decisions now. Further redraft will come following completed DPIA. 
* DPIA on Passenger Age/Jumio to OC? Or in-house following completion of Driver/Jumio OC?

Hi, please see our answers below:

# We will need to provide only *car registration numbers* (e.g. AA0001AA). We won’t share any other data.
# MIA will return the following data: car registration numbers (which we provided), speed limit violation (yes/no), time of speed limit violation (if any), place of speed limit violation (if any), amount of fine (if any).
# MIA will not provide any data about drivers, only about cars if they exceeded the speed limit. The information is reliable as it is the extraction from the system of automated speed limit control.
# Yes, correct. If we start getting this data from MIA we will be able to identify drivers who break the traffic rules, which can be dangerous both for passengers and the driver. 
# When we find out that a particular car that is registered at Bolt exceeded the speed limit, we will send communication to the driver linked to the car. We will inform the driver that we are aware of the speeding violation and remind the driver of safety standards and behavioral expectations. We will remind drivers that according to our Standard Terms and Conditions for drivers, all drivers must obey the traffic rules. At the first stage we won’t block such drivers if that’s their first case. If the driver exceeds the speed limit twice, we will send a reminder and say that next time his account will be temporarily blocked. For the third time, we will block driver account temporarily, depending on other metrics (history of blockings, driver’s average rating, complaints from riders).
# Exceeding the speed limit itself is not criminal offence, it’s administrative one. Criminal offence occurs only when people were injured (medium-high severity) or killed as a result of the traffic accident.

The red flag issue is that if Bolt UK is the recipient of the services and Majorel fail on the delivery of the services or breaches the terms of the MSA in its delivery, Bolt UK has no legal rights to enforce the contract with Majorel as its not a contracting party. 

Only Bolt Technology OU could enforce the right and there will be some complicated third party rights that will need to be employed to seek claims for damages or SLA breaches by Bolt UK through Bolt Technology OU to get to Majorel. {noformat}leandro@sqldb-ansible-new:~/git.sqldb/mysql-ansible$ cat auto_ghost.yaml
# Run with ssh agent forwarding to be able to clone git repo using your ssh key
# shell> ansible-playbook -i ec2.py --ssh-common-args='-o ForwardAgent=yes' foo.yaml
#
# ! REMEMBER to adjust 'hosts' and 'vars:' as needed
---
#- hosts: tag_shard_order
- hosts: tag_shard_aaaleandro
  become: no
  gather_facts: yes
  vars:
    git_repo_location: '/home/leandro/gh-ost_INFRA_XXXX'
    alter_DB: 'test_schema'
    alter_TABLE: 'test_table'
    alter_FILE: 'auto_ghost.sql'
    async_wait_time: 999999
  tasks:

    # TODO: only test with one cluster/shard (eg: order_afr), should work with multi shard but needs testing

    - block:
      - name: git clone gh-ost scripts
        ansible.builtin.git:
          repo: 'git@builder.internal:mysql-osc'
          dest: "{{ git_repo_location }}"
          accept_hostkey: yes

      - name: repopulate alter.sql from local source
        copy:
          src: "{{alter_FILE}}"
          dest: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sql"

      - name: make alter.sh executable
        file:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          mode: u+x,g+x,o+x

      - name: change alter.sh DB NAME
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'DB=taxify_fraud'
          replace: "DB={{alter_DB}}"

      - name: change alter.sh DB TABLE
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'TABLE=driver_period_check'
          replace: "TABLE={{alter_TABLE}}"

      - name: find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES prepare other node hostname
        set_fact:
          other_db_node: "{{ inventory_hostname | regex_replace('^(.*)-d2$', '\\1-d1') }}"
          #other_db_node: "au-d1"

      - name: find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES query read_only on other node
        become: yes
        shell: $( which mysql ) --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -BN -e "SELECT @@read_only;"
        delegate_to: "{{ other_db_node }}"
        register: is_replica

      - name: find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES set correct replica to monitor
        set_fact:
          other_db_node: "{{ other_db_node | regex_replace('^(.*)-d1$', '\\1-d3') }}"
        when: is_replica.stdout == "0"

      - name: change alter.sh MONITOR_SLAVES
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'MONITOR_SLAVES="xxx.sqldb,xxx.sqldb"'
          replace: "MONITOR_SLAVES=\"{{inventory_hostname}}.sqldb,{{other_db_node}}.sqldb\""

      - name: dry run gh-ost
        become: yes
        shell: "cd {{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/ ; ./alter.sh 2>&1 | tee dryrun_alter_`date +%Y-%m-%d_%H_%M_%S`.log"
        register: ghost_dryrun

      - debug: var=ghost_dryrun.stdout_lines

      - name: check table size in megabytes
        become: yes
        shell: "du --block-size 1m /mysql/data/{{alter_DB}}/{{alter_TABLE}}.ibd | awk '{print $1}'"
        register: table_size

      - name: check free space in kilobytes
        become: yes
        shell: "df --block-size 1m --output=avail /mysql | tail -n1 | awk '{print $1}'"
        register: disk_free

      - name:
        fail:
          msg: /mysql does not have the minimum space required to continue {{disk_free.stdout}} MB < 2 * {{table_size.stdout}} MB
        when: disk_free.stdout|int < 2*table_size.stdout|int

      - name: add execute option to alter.sh
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: '(--verbose \\)\s+#(--execute)'
          replace: '--verbose --execute'
      when: inventory_hostname.endswith('-d2')


    # had to run pause outside of block since pause module only runs on the first host of the group
    - pause:
        prompt: "Are you sure you want live run gh-ost (yes/no)"
      register: confirm_ghost
      delegate_to: localhost
      run_once: true

    - name: abort if user does not confirm
      meta: end_play
      when: confirm_ghost.user_input|lower != 'yes'


    - block:
      - name: LIVE run gh-ost
        shell: "cd {{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/ ; ./alter.sh 2>&1 | tee run_alter_`date +%Y-%m-%d_%H_%M_%S`.log"
        become: yes
        async: "{{ async_wait_time }}"
        poll: 0
        register: ghost_liverun

      - debug: var=ghost_liverun

        # THIS IS NOT NEEDED UNLESS WE WANT TO BLOCK WAITING FOR GH-OST TO COMPLETE
#      - name: check if gh-ost is complete
#        async_status:
#          jid: "{{ ghost_liverun.ansible_job_id }}"
#        register: job_result
#        until: job_result.finished
#        retries: 9000
#        delay: 60
#        become: yes

      - name: wait 20 sec and show just started gh-ost status
        shell: "sleep 20; echo status | /bin/nc -U /tmp/gh-ost.{{alter_DB}}.{{alter_TABLE}}.sock"
        become: yes
        register: ghost_live_status

      - debug: var=ghost_live_status.stdout_lines

      - debug:
          msg:
            - "Usefull Monitoring links, adjust hostname as needed:"
            - "Orchestrator: http://o.sqldb/web/clusters/"
            - "PMM MySQL Single Cluster View: http://pmm.sqldb/graph/d/GS0I5vrGk/mysql-single-cluster-view?orgId=1&refresh=5s&from=now-30m&to=now&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-region=All&var-environment=All&var-cluster=order-au&var-replication_set=All&var-node_name=All&var-service_name=All&var-node_id=&var-agent_id=&var-service_id=%2Fservice_id%2F3b276da9-59b5-4788-a244-75fe0fae27e5&var-az=&var-node_type=All&var-node_model=&var-database=All&var-service_type=All&var-username=All&var-schema=All"
            - "PMM InnoDB Metrics: http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/mysql-table-usage/mysql-table-usage?orgId=1&from=1620306116856&to=1620309716856&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-node_name=au-d1&var-cluster=order-au&var-service_name=All&var-schema=All&var-version=5.7.28-31&var-crop_service=au-d1-mysql&var-crop_host=au-d1&var-environment=All&var-replication_set=All&var-database=All&var-node_type=All&var-service_type=All&var-username=All"
            - "PMM MySQL Table Usage: http://pmm2.sqldb/graph/d/mysql-table-usage/mysql-table-usage?orgId=1&from=1620306116856&to=1620309716856&var-interval=$__auto_interval_interval&var-node_name=au-d1&var-cluster=order-au&var-service_name=All&var-schema=All&var-version=5.7.28-31&var-crop_service=au-d1-mysql&var-crop_host=au-d1&var-environment=All&var-replication_set=All&var-database=All&var-node_type=All&var-service_type=All&var-username=All"

      - debug:
          msg:
            - "WARNING! gh-ost is running in the background: {{alter_DB}}.{{alter_TABLE}}"
            - "When ready for cut-over, manually remove the /tmp/ghost.postpone.flag file."

      - debug:
          msg:
            - "Run the following command inside d2 gh-ost slave to check current status:"
            - "echo status | /bin/nc -U /tmp/gh-ost.{{alter_DB}}.{{alter_TABLE}}.sock"

      when: inventory_hostname.endswith('-d2')

---

- hosts: tag_shard_aaaleandro
  any_errors_fatal: true
  become: no
  gather_facts: yes
  vars:
    git_repo_location: '/home/leandro/gh-ost_INFRA_XXXX'
    alter_DB: 'test_schema'
    alter_TABLE: 'test_table'
    alter_FILE: 'auto_ghost.sql'
    async_wait_time: 999999
  tasks:

    # TODO: only test with one cluster/shard (eg: order_afr), should work with multi shard but needs testing

    # PRECHECKS:
    # - disk space in all cluster nodes
    # - binlog format in all cluster nodes
    - name: check table size in megabytes
      become: yes
      shell: "du --block-size 1m /mysql/data/{{alter_DB}}/{{alter_TABLE}}.ibd | awk '{print $1}'"
      register: table_size

    - name: check free space in kilobytes
      become: yes
      shell: "df --block-size 1m --output=avail /mysql | tail -n1 | awk '{print $1}'"
      register: disk_free

    - name: abort if not enough free disk space
      fail:
        msg: /mysql does not have the minimum space required to continue {{disk_free.stdout}} MB < 2 * {{table_size.stdout}} MB
      when: disk_free.stdout|int < 2*table_size.stdout|int

    - name: check binlog format is set to ROW
      become: yes
      shell: $( which mysql ) --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -BN -e "SELECT @@binlog_format;"
      register: binlog_format

    - name: abort if binlog format is not set to ROW
      fail:
        msg: ABORTING - binlog format is not set to ROW
      when: binlog_format.stdout !='ROW'

    # DEPLOY AND DRY RUN ON D2
    # comaster setup is checked here
    - block:

      - name: d2 - find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES prepare other node1 hostname
        set_fact:
          other_db_node1: "{{ inventory_hostname | regex_replace('^(.*)-d2$', '\\1-d1') }}"

      - name: d2 - find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES prepare other node3 hostname
        set_fact:
          other_db_node3: "{{ inventory_hostname | regex_replace('^(.*)-d2$', '\\1-d3') }}"

      - name: get read_only on other node1
        become: yes
        shell: $( which mysql ) --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -BN -e "SELECT @@read_only;"
        delegate_to: "{{ other_db_node1 }}"
        register: is_replica1

      - name: get read_only on other node3
        become: yes
        shell: $( which mysql ) --defaults-file=/etc/mysql/debian.cnf -BN -e "SELECT @@read_only;"
        delegate_to: "{{ other_db_node3 }}"
        register: is_replica3

      - name: abort if comaster setup is enabled
        fail:
          msg: ABORTING - found comaster setup
        when: is_replica1.stdout == "0" and is_replica3.stdout == "0"

      - name: d2 - git clone gh-ost scripts
        ansible.builtin.git:
          repo: 'git@builder.internal:mysql-osc'
          dest: "{{ git_repo_location }}"
          accept_hostkey: yes

      - name: d2 - repopulate alter.sql from local source
        copy:
          src: "{{alter_FILE}}"
          dest: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sql"

      - name: d2 - make alter.sh executable
        file:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          mode: u+x,g+x,o+x

      - name: d2 - change alter.sh DB NAME
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'DB=taxify_fraud'
          replace: "DB={{alter_DB}}"

      - name: d2 - change alter.sh DB TABLE
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'TABLE=driver_period_check'
          replace: "TABLE={{alter_TABLE}}"

      - name: find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES replica d3 to monitor
        set_fact:
          monitor_replica: "{{ other_db_node1 | regex_replace('^(.*)-d1$', '\\1-d3') }}"
        when: is_replica1.stdout == "0" and is_replica3.stdout == "1"

      - name: find suitable MONITOR_SLAVES replica d1 to monitor
        set_fact:
          monitor_replica: "{{ other_db_node1 }}"
        when: is_replica1.stdout == "1" and is_replica3.stdout == "0"
     
      - name: d2 - change alter.sh MONITOR_SLAVES
        replace:
          path: "{{ git_repo_location }}/gh-ost/alter.sh"
          regexp: 'MONITOR_SLAVES="xxx.sqldb,xxx.sqldb"'
          replace: "MONITOR_SLAVES=\"{{inventory_hostname}}.sqldb,{{monitor_replica}}.sqldb\""

      - name: d2 - dry run gh-ost
        become: yes

The legal scrutiny process took longer than anticipated in the beginning and ventured well outside strictly legal part into a security and tech part. However, have now gone through a essential stages of understanding risk and its intensity and am extending legal advise on the matter.

*TL;DR:*

*practise of scraping price data (accessible only through account creation) from RH platforms when done on regular and/or large scale creates very clear and well pronounced legal risks.* 

*→ These are largely indefensible from a legal perspective. Meaning that if any of scrapped competitors were to identify scraping + Bolt behind it -  it is 75%+ chance of Bolt loosing a case.*

*→ Only legal defence available: pushing all/majority of risk onto a service provider. This does not allow to avoid legal risk, and Bolt would still be in a firing line for legal sanctions and lawsuits from competitors, but tough indemnity rules in Service Contracts would give a chance to pass any damage sustained by Bolt onto a service provider. Service providers are extremely unlikely to accept transfer of any meaningful part of such risk though.*

*Only credible way to address Legal risks - is through non-legal tools: careful vendor scrutiny + scrutiny of used-tech + assurances on tight control of scraping protocol + liability transfer in cases of vendor failures.*

*In detail*

_Legal aspects_

Unlike scraping in standard e-commerce set-up where a truly public info (like catalogue, pricing) is being scraped without a need to opt-into applicable T&Cs, scraping in RH set-up, where all scraped info is accessible only through a dedicated user-account (and thus after signing a contract) - poses more intense legal risk:

* _breach of target’s T&Cs_ (checked e.g. Uber has a clear scraping prohibition, other bigger players are likely to have similar language);
* _breach of target’s DataBase right:_ while price point on its own is not a protected piece of info, entire pricing database and model - is. When you scrape regularly and on large scale, you do statistically significant inroads into target’s pricing model that allows you to ‘extract and re-build’ its pricing database. And this is prohibited by law and confirmed by recent case-law.

All the legal argument to defend against such claims like _it is public info; we did not copy it entirely; we did not re-use it in its entirety to build our business_ have been often rejected by courts in similar cases.

All in all fact that pricing-model is not easily available to the world at large; the fact that it is walled-off for registered users; the fact that frequent scraping is needed to get commercial benefit out of that; the fact that it is prohibited by T&Cs; the fact that full pricing picture is kept confidential → makes it easy for targets to prove a case that scraper is in breach of its Database Right and thus should compensate damages. Good news here is that Bolt is in exact same position and has good legal grounds to go after scrapers itself 🙂 

_Traceability aspects: non-legal defence_

If scraping is detected by target and finger is pointed to an actual scraper (aka scraping service provider) - it is very likely to  quickly point a finger at beneficiary of scraping (seeking to avoid large financial exposure and mandated by court). And even thus Bolt would bot be doing it directly - it would still be held liable.

For Bolt to escape this risk there would be 2 avenues: 

* Transfer risk to a Vendor itself claiming that it should fully ensure air-tight set-up of its practise. There are few issues with that: Bolt in any case would be named as client and would be exposed to reputation damage (no way around it) + no vendor is likely to accept full risk transfer (it would be capped in any case and these caps are unlikely to absorb full financial exposure).
* Ensure that neither vendor, nor Bolt is identifiable in the first place: this is a non-legal tool controlling the risk through tight protocols; state-of-art tech set-up/tools. And since Bolt would not be doing it directly and using a third-party - success of deploying this tools depends largely on vendor selection process and vendor management process.

If target is capable of spotting scraping activity: not done in a “natural and neutral” way, it will be capable of associating scraping to a particular account. If accounts used are in any way containing identifiable data (devices used to create and operate account point to identifiable meta data; user names used; card details used to set accounts; locations from where accounts are accessed - like if it is Estonia it will be clear it is Bolt) → it could point back to Vendor or even Bolt. Other weak points could be: scraping Target in markets where only Bolt and Target are operating - this would easily point to Bolt and give a sense for target what to look for / how to get evidence of Bolt being behind; how the data is channeled back to Bolt - could that be in any way interfered and detected.

Basically any aspects where Vendor scraping protocols interact with the real world give rise to exposure. The way to address this risk is to very well understand the proposed solution, its tech-side; do a proper scrutiny internally + get assurances around its un-treaceability. This requires well structured and tight vendor selection and management process, involving not only ops + legal teams, but also engineering.

An initial assessment with help of engineering was done vis-a-vis CGS. This does not reveal any clear gaps in the approach. However, it was clear that level of detail we have is not sufficient to do this properly and does not re-assure on traceability. [~accountid:605463a8686bf500704dbecf]  has thus put together a draft detailed vendor questionnaire to extract more details.

*Proposal how to move forward:*

* assess from _potential cost vs. potential benefit angle_. What impact on GMV deployment of scraping may yield and compare this against risk intensity (after going through Vendor dd)

* Deep dive into Vendor proposal and scrutinise set-ups involving engineering. AKA go through a proper vendor and their tech due-diligence;
* if comfortable with any solution - negotiate transfer of at least some risk to the Vendor as an essential commercial term.

Legal can assist with the risk-transfer negotiation point of course and general legal scrutiny, the vendor due-diligence should be carried out by the supply team leaning onto engineering. While general cost vs. benefit decision is probably for vertical leadership to make.

Happy to discuss this in a call\!

* 11:24:16

* 11:24:28

* 11:24:32

* 11:24:33

** app sends getFinishedRideSummary and shows RatingScreen

Hi Silja,

The question is do we have to go through these questionnaires. Not sure if my colleagues have clearly stated the situation, but the phone conversation recording is a MUST for a car-sharing business line. We provide access to our users to assets worth 20k Eur or even more expensive, the whole user identification is purely digital and we rely on 3rd party service provider. We also provide to our 3rd party customer support access to unlock/lock the vehicles, etc. Agents have to identify users over the phone, ask for their personal sensitive information: name, last name, last 4 digits of personal code, etc.

Phone recording is mainly needed to have the evidence in case of any fraud and is coming from my previous experience running CityBee car-sharing for 5 years, plus provides a tool to track the quality of our phone support. 

Regarding the fraud, I already had a situation where on the first week of the launch of service I called our customer support and asked to unlock the car, any car was unlocked for me without carrying any identification, and I was just behaving very politely. It is one thing that our partners were not following all the processes, but there will be cases where people will try to game the system in many ways: fraud with fuel cards, fraud with the cars, etc. If we do not have any evidence we're in a very risky situation. Also, let's keep in mind that customer support agent rotation is also very high, we will have new agents joining constantly.

IMO, phone recording is quite common practice, especially with the cases where users need to be identified over the phone and there's a higher level of risk. The most important thing is to inform the user before the call that it will be recorded and if the user agrees then just proceeds further. If not, well then the user has to hang up the phone.

Hi,

*DPO ADVICE*

We likely have a breach of the security principle in the UK GDPR where ‘appropriate technical and organisational measures’ (i.e. the verification/authentication check) has not been undertaken.

I’ve listened to the inbound call and can, thankfully, hear no disclosure of information which would meet a threshold of harm to the legitimate account holder.

On attempting to listen to the outbound call - here [https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/20811172|https://bolt.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/20811172] - it is not loading. I’m still uncertain what account information was shared. 

If all that was disclosed was, indeed, information concerning the cancellation fee(s) - and thereby confirming to a third party details of a booking and cancellation - then this is most certainly a breach. But should no compliant have in turn been received by the legitimate account holders then it seems fair to assume that the likelihood of any harm, with all the information available, appears to be a minimal loss of privacy.


*ACTIONS*

# Can you please escalate immediately should a complaint from the account holder be received about the loss of privacy so that, with context, a full harms assessment can be carried out?
# Should there be any further suspicious attempts made to access information from the accounts in this instance, please let us know. This is crucial should we be made aware of a systematic campaign to gain information illegally by the caller to these specific accounts.
# Please immediately have the agent undertake all necessary data protection training and undertake rehearsal/practise calls with a team lead/manager to ensure they know the verification checks to be undertaken. 
# Please ensure that the agent recognises the risks associated with providing account details to unauthorised third parties e.g. that’s to say that a third party seeking information from another account may, for example, be an abusive partner attempting to track/control/manipulate their spouse, or a bad actor attempting to hoover enough information to commit fraud etc etc. Verification checks are not optional. Please re-assure the agent that if feeling pressured on a call specifically, or if workload is having them ‘skip corners’ then they should consult with team leads/managers.


*CONCLUSION*


With all the information available this breach does meet the threshold for external notification to the regulatory authority, namely, the ICO, nor to the account holders themselves. Please note this advice may change should further information come to light; if access attempts are made on the account again; or if the named agent in this instance again fails to undertake a verification check in any other instance.

* *Consultation space*
** Is a voluntary meeting

** Is held only when there are specific issues/questions to be discussed

** Is a voluntary meeting
** Reoccurs once a month
** Can be shared with the whole CM team
** Is meant for presenting a project or how a real issue was solved and discussing the results afterwards
** Everybody from the team can be a presenter
*** Being a presenter is voluntary
** Meeting notes are documented in Confluence and the presentations are recorded

** Can be prepared as a Slack post for our team or be a part of the team syncs (TBD)

*** If no volunteers, Content Strategists prepare the learning pill

*** The first topics to address can be related to how to use Looker and spreadsheets, how to form a hypothesis, basic statistics, etc.

[~accountid:6017bc19dc29b4006a7f1025] might have more expertise/experience in this area and add to this, but it sounds like the timings are very tight so he might not have time.

*Purchasing the EV* - Afraid I’m not a tax expert (you might be better off also checking this with a member of the Bolt Finance/Tax team) but +broadly I can’t see that there is a “tax” issue for Bolt or the driver+. Assuming the following applies:

* Bolt purchases the EV outright (you’ll pay VAT on the purchase and defer to Bolt’s tax/finance team on if this can be claimed back considering it’s an EV). When the EV is gifted to the winner as far as I’m aware there’s no tax on gifts in the UK. For completeness, as the entrants (drivers) are not employees this will not be considered a taxable benefit, again caveat that I’m not a tax expert(\!). 
* Considering road tax - I believe in the UK you cannot transfer road tax and Bolt will need to tax the vehicle (which you can then get a refund for once ownership of the vehicle is transferred) and the winner will also need to tax vehicle on receipt. I haven’t had a chance to check this but I imagine road tax for EV is very low/zero. See my points below on the giveaway regarding specifying that the winner taxes, insures and transfers ownership of the EV. 

*Running the Giveaway* - Assuming drivers/entrants do not have to pay to enter and it’s run as a free prize draw (i.e. not regulated as a lottery) you will need to comply with general advertising rules and not mislead the entrants. You will need to make the conditions of entry very clear (e.g. timings, dates, timezone, whether the driver needs to already be registered/completed trips etc., how the winner will be contacted, Bolt employees can’t enter, entrants 18+, full UK driving licence etc.) and set out how the winner will be picked and the car delivered/collected. Other things to consider - what if a new driver enters and wins and doesn’t continue driving with Bolt, you’ve probably considered the commercial points/benefits of this giveaway already. 

I hope this is all helpful\! FYI - I’m part time at Bolt and will update my Slack status with when I’m online for Bolt.

Evaluation Model:

Phase 1 - reaction:

* This level measures how learners have reacted to the training, the relevance and usefulness of the training.
* Survey to include soft skills feedback on training (video and assessment). This could be included in the ‘survey of the day' (however, more time needed to extract info as some days may not have soft skills training).
* Alternatively, a survey to be completed after the day’s soft skill training (possibly of 2 soft skills training on one day - dependent on the onboarding structure.
* Feeback to be gathered during CoS by trainer/s. Information to be shared with the responsible L&D team member (for example Piotr - Majorel). Feedback to include agent engagement, discussion points about the soft skills training, positives and negatives. Structured questions to be created to ensure uniformity across both verticals.
* At the end of phase 1, we should have a good understanding of how well the training was received and determine any gaps in the training content.

Phase 2 - Learnings

* Measure the knowledge and skills gained by learners as a result of the training.
* Measure test scores for each soft skills topic.
* Measure fail/pass rate
* Possibly include overall survey question/s in the onboarding survey. 
* At this stage of evaluation, you will be able to determine if the training is meeting its set objectives, what are the specific skills that can be developed with this training, and the scope for improvements in content and method of delivery.

Phase 3 - Behaviour

* Checking CSATs monthly for a specific period (3 months)
* MKAs - performance /  outliers
* Share information monthly along with MKA results (specific for new joiners)
* Focus groups - mid-way point - schedule time with new joiners and discuss onboarding (leading more to soft skills topics)
* Understand how the training has impacted the learner’s performance and attitude at work.

Phase 4 - Results

* New joiners for each month to be reviewed in the onboarding monthly report (after onboarding was completed). While this is/should be done normally, this can be added for managers to monitor.
* Monitor and share results of new joiner’s journey each month for 3 months (can be longer if needed) with managers.

Hi [~accountid:6038f47f783a46006895f14d] @Ismael

The proposed lease is a material deviation from the majority of our standard positions for property. However having spoken to Ismael, I do recognise that the positions are aligned with local market practice and the competition that exists for acquiring suitable warehouses for the storage of e-scooters and such devices.

I also note that we have been in discussions with the broker and landlord already and that this has only just come to legal. We really needed to be part of the dialogue beforehand, not at the final stage where we are left with sub-optimal legal terms and a challenging commercial position.

A couple of comments:

*Broker: CBRE*

What specifications was provided to the broker and why is their fee so expensive? When we use brokers in the UK, we try and cap the fee to no more than 1 month’s rent which we make the landlord pay for acquiring Bolt as a tenant. Is this not the case for Bordeaux? If this is standard practice then I would like to be included much earlier on in the negotiation next time as we would have had to sign the broker’s engagement terms and I do not recall seeing this.

*Lease Terms*

(1) I note that the minimum term is three years. There doesn’t seem to be any flexibility as we cannot terminate prior to this date even if we serve 1 years notice. Given that our business changes from time to time, we will need some form of termination for convenience clause and we should negotiate a long notice period. 

The alternative is accepting the financial liability of the the premise for 3 years even though we many not use if for a period of time. 

(2) There is no ability to assign or sub-let the lease to a new tenant without permission. This is a poor mitigation strategy in trying to get rid of the property that we do not want if the business changes but at least we have an option (although at the landlord’s discretion). 

In reality this may be acceptable if real estate for a scooter warehouse is in demand due to the rarity of such properties. However, the big concern is that Bolt will have to become a joint and several guarantor for the successor of the lease. This means we could be liable for the rent a competitor (that we’ve sub-leased the warehouse to), if they refuse to pay or go bankrupt. This is not a good position. We can deal with such issues when we sub-lease the property but I rather we remove the obligation from the lease now otherwise this will be a problem in the future. Can this be discussed with the landlord. 

(3) There are extensive maintenance and repairing obligations (Section 2, Section 3, Section 10) - If we are to accept this lease, we should ask the broker / landlord to disclose the most recent survey / inspection of the building to determine the condition of the property. We would also need to see the landlord’s maintenance and repairing plans for the next 1 -3 years so we can be sure they are not proposing a major replacement of anything (such as the roof or air-conditioning units etc.) where they would hold us liability for a material contribution on cost. Please can you obtain this?

(4) Please identify all the taxes that would be payable on the lease of this building. The Special Conditions are particularly useful in terms of setting our the immediate costs owed to the landlord but are there any addition business or property tax rates owed to any third party that needs to be identified.

[~accountid:5cf7cf76840f290e75625425] - It seems to me that there is very limited choice in Bordeaux and if the broker has identified that this is a reasonable option (given our specification), it may require that we create a specific property profile for this region so that additional requests are aligned. This position is similar to what we are finding in Germany where landlords have greater bargaining power than the tenants leaving us to consider a higher risk profile. 

The lease itself isn’t too bad but does place a lot of financial obligation on Bolt. If the business is willing to absorb the additional P&L business risk of the property lease to move forward and we can get answers to the queries above, we could move forward.

_debrief on Latvia, essentially Karlis is requesting permission to place a Bolt acquired cover for the fleet operating on the platform with the following features:_

# _Bolt enters into a group purchasing agreement_
# _Each driver has option to take up cover through Bolt_
# _Each subscribing car requires declaration to attach cover_
# _Upon attachment Bolt takes up annual premium obligation for the each car_
# _Drivers are charged on a periodic basis to distribute premiums._
# _If driver departs and stops paying Bolt will remain liable for the premiums due_
# _Bolt is simply aggregating purchasing and passing through the cost of the insurance, not brokering or taking a fee on the placement_
# _Bolt it taking up a standard cover and offering access to the same, there is no negotiation taking place_

_There are a couple of things that cause me slight concern._

# _Can Bolt be seen as conducting a regulated role? (I think the risk is low but would like to be sure we are not going to be fined for acting as a Broker)._
# _Can Bolt be held liable by driver if insurance fails to perform/cover an incident whether on the grounds of an excluded loss or financial incapacity of the carrier? (Again I think the risk is low however occurs to me that we are offering a product, if the product is deemed defective we are the party who has sourced and "sold" it)._
# _Is there a reclassification risk results from this? (Again and pointing to the commentary we saw in London I believe the risk is low)._
# _There a danger of our attracting only the low quality and therefore high risk drivers under this construct, which will not be obligatory and may only be attractive to drivers who cannot access good quality insurance directly themselves. This could have a carry over effect on the experience of riders and the public at large. (I'm mindful that perhaps the cover should only be offered to drivers with whom we have a track and they have a sound driver rating)._

2. Header does not jump when you simply tap on buttons. In screen recording above I’m intentionally pressing finger on the button, and, while pressed, I’m moving it off the button - pan gesture to the top - to show the highlighted state of the suggestion. It it this pan gesture that causes header to “jump”, because it is treated as an attempt to scroll the chat. [~accountid:5e0f0e7f0242870e996ebba8], do we really need to change this behaviour?
3.1. About message size: at the time of showing message in “Sending” state we do not know message timestamp yet, as it would be received from backend later, when backend responds with “ok, I’m accepting you message”-response. So, at “Sending” state we can not correctly calculate the width of unknown timestamp. I see two workarounds we can have here:
* the first one would be to use current local time to calculate approximate width of a timestamp, and use this value as a gap - this would trigger message resizing for some (presumably small) amount of messages anyway, as backend-generated timestamp could differ from what we used for “Sending” state;
* the second workaround would be to have a fixed width of timestamp label being set to the maximum possible width of all possible timestamp values - but this is really non-trivial task, because we support interface translations with numerals rendered differently from {{1}}, {{2}}, {{3}} and so on (e.g. Arabic language - [https://omniglot.com/language/numbers/arabic.htm|https://omniglot.com/language/numbers/arabic.htm|smart-link]). And also user’s locale settings could affect the timestamp (e.g. 12-hour or 24-hour format, presence of {{AM}} and {{PM}} suffixes, etc.). And I don’t really know a good way to calculate this fixed width for timestamp in a general way, that should work for any given language and any given locale settings. The only general option I see is to calculate the width for all possible timestamps in runtime, and select the widest one. But this is definitely a hacky thing to do.
So, [~accountid:5e0f0e7f0242870e996ebba8], what do you think is a better solution here?

Confirmed information:

h3. Additional information about the verification process

h3. *What is* *_user verification process_**?*

Verification process is a process needed to identify the user and make sure we can allow them to use our services. The possible reasons for the user verification:

* Legal requirements, e.g. we need to verify the user to proceed with the account deletion and data sharing requests
* Potential fraud, e.g. when our internal fraud system detects suspicious activity, we need to verify the user to make sure they are a real person.

h3. *What is* *_manual verification_**?*

Manual verification is a process when a CS agent manually verifies the user by clicking the Verify button on the rider Admin account. Manual verification follows either:

* Successful external verification by Veriff or Jumio (in the markets where Veriff or Jumio are used)
* Internal verification of the user (the UK)
* Internal verification of the user's documents by CS agents (other markets).

As a result of the manual verification, the user’s fraud score is set to be either 0 or positive. The _Verification_ row and the note _Manual verification – (date, time) there_ will appear on the user’s Admin profile.

h3. *What is* *_forced user verification_**?*

Forced user verification is in place for the cases when we must verify user documents due to legal regulations. Currently, forced verification is enabled for the following countries and business lines:

* Bolt Drive in Estonia: we verify driving licence to confirm they are eligible to drive a car
* Bolt Scooters in Norway: we verify the user documents to confirm their age.

Forced verification does not affect a user’s fraud score.

h3. *What are the external verification providers?*

Currently, we use Veriff and Jumio. These providers do not have integration with our fraud system. Once the verification is completed by the providers, we use their answer to decide whether we can proceed with the manual verification in Admin.

Jumio is integrated with our Admin so that the verified users are allowed to use the rental services (Bolt Drive in Estonia and Bolt scooters in Norway). But this verification does not affect a user’s fraud score.

I can’t say precisely how restrictive you can be but the guiding principle with most jurisdictions is that the restriction has to be reasonable given the economic circumstances and the business that the entity is involved in. For example:

* You cannot have an outright restriction from an entity providing their services to other third parties (whether competitors or not) if that’s their core business especially if you are not a large customer or account for most of their sales volumes. This will be tantamount to a restriction of their freedom to trade.
* If their core mandate is providing a particular service ONLY to ride hailing companies- it would also be unfair to restrict them from providing this service to Bolt competitors. 
* if they are able to provide services from various locations you can restrict where they should provide your services from if you want to avoid cross pollination with a competitor’s information.

determine pass abuser type

{code:sql}with user_first_pass_purchase as 
(
select user_id, min(created) first_subscription_bought
from rental.rental_order_subscription_purchase sp
where payment_status = 'captured'
group by 1
),
tables as (
SELECT 
	o.user_id, 
	u.created as user_created,
	ufpp.first_subscription_bought,
	date_diff('day',user_created,first_subscription_bought) user_created_to_first_pass_bought_days,
	count(DISTINCT o.id) count_all_rides, 
	count(DISTINCT case when fsp.name like 'Daily%' then  os.id else null end) count_sub_rides_daily,
	count(DISTINCT case when fsp.name like 'Weekly%' then  os.id else null end) count_sub_rides_weekly,
	count(DISTINCT case when fsp.name like 'Monthly%' then  os.id else null end) count_sub_rides_monthly,
	1.0*count_sub_rides_daily/count_all_rides daily_pass_rides_share,
	CASE 
		WHEN daily_pass_rides_share=1 and user_created_to_first_pass_bought_days<3 then 'daily pass abuser 100%'
		WHEN daily_pass_rides_share=1 and user_created_to_first_pass_bought_days>=3 then 'daily pass abuser 90%'
		WHEN daily_pass_rides_share>=0.8 and daily_pass_rides_share<1 then 'daily pass abuser 75%'
		WHEN daily_pass_rides_share>=0.6 and daily_pass_rides_share<0.8 then 'daily pass abuser 50%'
		WHEN daily_pass_rides_share<0.6 then 'daily pass abuser 0%'
	END pass_abuser_type		
FROM rental.rental_order_order o 
LEFT JOIN rental.rental_order_order_with_subscription os ON o.id = os.ORDER_id AND o.connection_id = os.connection_id 
LEFT JOIN rental.rental_order_subscription_purchase sp ON os.subscription_id = sp.subscription_id 
LEFT JOIN rental.rental_fleet_subscription_pack fsp ON sp.subscription_pack_id = fsp.id
LEFT JOIN user_user u on o.user_id=u.id
JOIN user_first_pass_purchase ufpp on o.user_id=ufpp.user_id
WHERE o.city_id=386 AND o.state = 'finished' and o.created>date'2021-05-31' and o.created<date'2021-06-07'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
select pass_abuser_type, count(user_id), sum(count_all_rides)
from tables
group by 1
{code}

Below is Feedback from the client:

I have gone through the terms and conditions for business accounts for Bolt and Legal would require clarification and/or renegotiation from Bolt on some of the following clauses in their terms and conditions.

A. Ref Clause 5:1 - "Bolt does not offer transport services. It is also not a provider of transport agency service for finding Passengers for Drivers. Bolt shall not take any responsibility for the quality or the absence of defects in the provision of transport services by the Drivers. As the provision and availability of transport services depends on Drivers, Bolt cannot and does not guarantee that the availability of Drivers meets the needs of the Users."

Clarification 1: Our contractual relationship is with Bolt and not the drivers or a transport service company. Thus, if Bolt states that it shall not take any responsibility under clause 5:1, who shall take such responsibilities? It will be highly appreciated if the addendum can clearly state the Parties that will be responsible in the terms of quality and defects in the provision of services offered by Bolt. *While there is an agreement with Bolt in respect of invoicing and provision of access to the platform- the drivers are independent service providers who actually provide the transportation service so they are liable if there is any issue with the service provided. Bolt acts as intermediary and if there are complaints made by the customer based on their use of the platform and driver behaviour- Bolt will mediate between the driver and customer.* 

B. Ref Clause 5.3 - Bolt is not liable for any loss or damage that Customer or User may incur as a result of using Bolt Business, unless provided otherwise by law. The financial liability of Bolt in connection with the latter shall be limited to 500 euros. Bolt shall not be liable for the actions, errors or omissions of the Driver.

Clarification 2: The agreement is governed by the laws of Estonia but the business relationship is in Tanzania. Hence, how do we address liability for loss and damages that are recognized in Tanzania (since the business relationship is in Tanzania) but not recognized under the Estonian Law? We will appreciate it if Bolt can clarify, specify and detail the loss and damages that it will be liable for in the addendum. *The agreement is governed by Estonian law because the Bolt Platform is domiciled in Estonia. However, we can agree for governing law and dispute resolution to be in Tanzania. Bolt will be liable for payment related losses under our agreement while the driver will be liable for any incidents that happen during the trip e.g accidents.* 

Clarification 3: In the event that the loss or damage incurred by SPENN as a result of using Bolt Business exceeds 500 euros (e.g. loss of life, property, harm/injury causing defects to persons), what strategies has Bolt put in place to address such situations? *These losses will likely be as a result of an accident and these will be covered by the drivers insurance. Drivers are required to have third party insurance.* 

Clarification 4: Bearing in mind that our contractual relationship is with Bolt and not the drivers (we have no relationship whatsoever with the drivers), If Bolt will not be liable for actions, errors or omissions of the drivers, can Bolt clarify who will be liable for actions, errors or omissions of the drivers caused by the use of Bolt Business Services? *You do have a relationship with the drivers as they are the ones providing the transportation service and they will be liable for their actions, errors or omissions. Bolt’s role is to provide access to the platform and thus create a marketplace between the customer and the driver.* 

C. Ref Clause 6.5 - Bolt is entitled to terminate Agreement and block Customer’s access to Business Portal without prior notice in cases where Customer breaches this Agreement, any applicable laws or regulations, or harms Bolt’s brand, reputation or business

Renegotiation 5: We would require a prior notification as a business courtesy for us to understand why SPENN's access is blocked or agreement terminated and to help us rearrange our schedule as soon as possible. *Okay.* 

D. Ref Clause 7.5 - Agreement shall be governed by and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of Estonia. If a dispute resulting from Agreement could not be settled by the negotiations, then the dispute shall be finally settled in Harju County Court. 

Renegotiation 6: We have no knowledge of the Estonia Laws or Courts. Besides, our business relationship is in Tanzania. Hence, we will prefer the agreement to either be governed by the Laws of Tanzania or the Laws of England and Wales. We will also prefer to settle our disputes in either Tanzania or England and Wales. *We can provide for it to be governed by the Laws of Tanzania.*

* the Act ('law') itself, and

The statutory order is issued by The Ministry of Environment of Denmark and contains rules that elaborate or specify the rules in an Act. In this case the statutory order is i.a. laid down pursuant to section 51 b of the Danish Environmental Protection Act and specifies the further rules on shopping bags, including rules regarding minimum prices, materials and labelling. 

The statutory order is binding on citizens, companies and public authorities, like an Act.

The preparatoires/the legislative material are the explanatory notes accompanying the Act. The explanatory notes explain why the Act is being introduced and what it is about. There may be explanatory notes both on the Act in general and on the individual sections. The preparatoires/ the legislative material are thus used for the interpretation of the Act.

Hi Alex,

thanks again for your request relating to the WEEE registration for your e-Scooters.

Please find our *summary* on the registration requirement +*attached*+ and *high level comments* on the contracts +*as follows*+:

As a general remark, we would like to point out that both contracts are not aligned with the latest version of the Electrical and Electronic Equipment Act (“ElektroG”). The latest version has been implemented on 1 Janaury 2021. There are several references included in the service agreement (“Leistungsvertrag”) leading to false sections of the ElektroG for this reason, e.g. there are references to section 9 para 4 of the ElektroG in the preamble of the contract and also in appendix 1 with regard to collection groups which are, however, now listed in section 14 para 1 of the ElektroG. Section 3.4 of the contract provides for references to section 11 para 3 and section 12 of the ElektroG which is also not correct. The former provisions have been revised comprehensively. The contract on the proof of an insolvency-proof guarantee („Vertrag über den Nachweis einer insolvenzsicheren Garantie“) explicitly refers to the ElektroG in its version of 20/10/2015, which is outdated.

Thus, the references should be reviewed and the contracts adapted to the content of the current provisions, where necessary. We are of course happy to mark up the contracts in this regard. Please just let us know, if you want us to do this or prefer to discuss with WEEE Return GmbH whether a more recent version can be made available.

 

However, it should be verified first, whether Bolt actually is considered a manufacturer within the meaning of the ElektroG. Only if this is the case, Bolt has to register and what is more, comply with several substantial take-back, notification and documentation obligations the ElektroG provides for. In order to define the specific obligations, it is essential to fully understand the manufacturing / procurement process with regard to the e-Scooters. We have added questions in our summary in this respect and it would be helpful if you could provide us with the respective details.

Afterwards, we can properly assess whether the obligations intended to be transferred to WEE Return GmbH within the framework of the service agreement („Leistungsvertrag“) comply with Bolt’s legal obligations under the ElektroG.

As also mentioned in our summary, it might be worth noting already, that WEEE Return GmbH would act under a power of attorney, but will not (and is also not allowed to) take over the position of an authorised representative in accordance with section 8 of the ElektroG for Bolt. In case Bolt has no permanent establishment in Germany, a respective “ElektroG authorised representative” would have to be appointed.

Please also note that the e-Scooters contain batteries and that such batteries are regarded to be industrial batteries and, hence, give rise to the application of the German Batterie Act. The recycling requirements on such batteries are quite similar to those of the e-scooters. You can extend the registration for the e-scooters to the batteries used. We will fill in on the details, if you wish so.

The contracts must be adjusted, however and subject to the above, we have not identified material red flags.

Our memo will be proofread and revised with a view to additions to the Battery act tomorrow, hence, you will find attached only a draft version. The final version will be with you beginning next week.

Best regards

Svenja and Christoph

We confirm that handling cash _per se_ by the couriers is compliant under the T&C (both for Partners, especially please see points 7.1 and 7.6 and for Couriers, especially please see points 8.1 and 8.6), i.e. the T&C allow the drivers to accept cash payments and pay the cash back to the restaurants. Also, Polish civil law does not limit this possibility. It is also possible that the courier accepts cash payment from a customer and delivers the cash to BOLT, whereas BOLT pays the balance to the restaurant via bank transfer or otherwise. In such case the courier would act as intermediary during payment.  

From criminal law, it must be underlined that the cash received from the customers does not belong to the drivers and they are not entitled to use it in any way. Additionally, please note that if the drivers used the cash and later on repaid it back, there would be grounds to charge the cash payment with civil law transaction tax on basis similar as for loan agreements. Andrzej and his colleagues may expand on this matter if you need any further information relating to tax aspects of this payment mechanism.

Blue cells to set variables.Approach:


# Battery degrades. If battery has lower capacity, we start to pay more for charging per ride
# If we replace battery earlier, we to some extent avoid this, but we depreciate hardware then at a higher rate
# Other costs are not affected by battery decision.
# then we aim to find a battery capacity % after which we want to replace a battery, so that battery depreciation cost + 3PL cycle cost is minimal

I assume that battery has capacity of 10k rides, it gradually (but not linearly) declines, and after 10k rides it’s completely dead.
Then I calculate what would be the battery depreciation rate per ride per each consecutive 500 rides bucket in this 10k rides (it will be constant, but will heavily dependant on how early we replace battery)
Also I calculate the charging cycle per ride for each bucket. If we don’t replace battery, it grows. Depending on when we replace battery, at some point it ‘resets’ and starts from the beginning.I ungroup first 3 calculations (for 95/90/85) so that you have an idea how it’s calculated

*bottomline:*


# Obviously, the higher 3PL charging cycle cost, the earlier better to replace battery

# With given parameters and given battery degradation speed (you can adjust it by changing percents in C13-W13 cells. You can set what the capacity of battery will be after 500,1000,1500 etc rides):

* with 2 Eur we may want to replace battery at 60%
* with 3 Eur we may want to replace battery at 70%
* with 5-7 Eur we may want to replace battery at 70-80%
